source_user: Advanced cluster case GDR-42: Design a validation plan for GPUDirect RDMA between GPUs and NICs. Variant 42 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: verify topology and peer access, registration and pinning, IOMMU/container permissions, NIC-GPU affinity, direct versus staged copies, and compare bandwidth and CPU utilization. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Assume an authorized, isolated validation window with no production traffic, supported and documented GPU/NIC/driver/firmware combinations, stable power and thermal conditions, and a tested rollback path. These are assumptions to verify, not platform facts. For GDR variant 42, first record GPU/NIC PCIe topology, NUMA and process/NIC affinity, link state, peer-access capability, runtime/driver/firmware versions, IOMMU and container permissions, buffer registration and pinning results, queue/completion errors, and an instrumented indication that the transfer is GPU-direct rather than host-staged. A capability, permission, registration, or topology failure blocks a performance claim.

Hypothesis: with message sizes, buffer placement, concurrency, duration, software versions, and thermal conditions held fixed, a confirmed GPU-direct path improves effective bandwidth (GB/s) and/or reduces host CPU utilization versus an otherwise matched host-staged control, without worsening latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, or checksum correctness. Use warmups and randomized interleaved trials, synchronized transfer/completion timestamps, repeated samples, and report medians, percentiles, variance or confidence intervals, sample counts, and units. Record GPU/NIC utilization, CPU utilization, link counters, retries, queue depth, and registration overhead; separate setup from steady-state transfer time.

Before changing anything, take read-only configuration and counter snapshots and obtain authorization. Validate correctness with payload checksums and no dropped or reordered completions. Compare direct and staged paths under identical workloads and affinity, and include a negative/control case that deliberately disables or prevents direct access when safe. Do not infer directness from throughput alone. If direct access cannot be proved, measurements are evidence about an unverified or staged path only. Stop and restore the prior configuration on data-integrity errors, repeated completion/transport failures, unsafe temperatures, production impact, or a predefined regression threshold (for example, a statistically credible latency-tail increase or bandwidth loss beyond the agreed margin). Preserve logs, exact commands, versions, topology, raw samples, and provenance so another operator can reproduce the result; mark unsupported or missing evidence as evidence_required rather than filling it in.

quality_dimensions.measurement_rigor: units, synchronized timestamps, randomized interleaving, repetitions, percentiles, uncertainty, and raw evidence
quality_dimensions.safety_and_limits: authorization, read-only collection first, correctness gates, stop conditions, and no invented platform facts

risks: GPUDirect may be unsupported, permission-blocked, or silently fall back to host staging.
Throughput-only evidence can misattribute topology, CPU, thermal, congestion, or setup effects.
Changing IOMMU, container, driver, or production network settings can cause outage or security impact.

versions, peer-access and registration/pinning results
direct-path instrumentation and matched staged-control measurements
raw synchronized samples with units, percentiles, uncertainty, and checksums
authorization, rollback record, and error/counter logs

source_user: Advanced cluster case GDR-52: Design a validation plan for GPUDirect RDMA between GPUs and NICs. Variant 52 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: verify topology and peer access, registration and pinning, IOMMU/container permissions, NIC-GPU affinity, direct versus staged copies, and compare bandwidth and CPU utilization. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Assume an authorized, isolated validation window with no production traffic, supported and documented GPU/NIC/driver/firmware combinations, stable power and thermal conditions, and a tested rollback path. These are assumptions to verify, not platform facts. For GDR variant 52, first record GPU/NIC PCIe topology, NUMA and process/NIC affinity, link state, peer-access capability, runtime/driver/firmware versions, IOMMU and container permissions, buffer registration and pinning results, queue/completion errors, and an instrumented indication that the transfer is GPU-direct rather than host-staged. A capability, permission, registration, or topology failure blocks a performance claim.

Hypothesis: with message sizes, buffer placement, concurrency, duration, software versions, and thermal conditions held fixed, a confirmed GPU-direct path improves effective bandwidth (GB/s) and/or reduces host CPU utilization versus an otherwise matched host-staged control, without worsening latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, or checksum correctness. Use warmups and randomized interleaved trials, synchronized transfer/completion timestamps, repeated samples, and report medians, percentiles, variance or confidence intervals, sample counts, and units. Record GPU/NIC utilization, CPU utilization, link counters, retries, queue depth, and registration overhead; separate setup from steady-state transfer time.

Before changing anything, take read-only configuration and counter snapshots and obtain authorization. Validate correctness with payload checksums and no dropped or reordered completions. Compare direct and staged paths under identical workloads and affinity, and include a negative/control case that deliberately disables or prevents direct access when safe. Do not infer directness from throughput alone. If direct access cannot be proved, measurements are evidence about an unverified or staged path only. Stop and restore the prior configuration on data-integrity errors, repeated completion/transport failures, unsafe temperatures, production impact, or a predefined regression threshold (for example, a statistically credible latency-tail increase or bandwidth loss beyond the agreed margin). Preserve logs, exact commands, versions, topology, raw samples, and provenance so another operator can reproduce the result; mark unsupported or missing evidence as evidence_required rather than filling it in.
